answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits show fabricated work or collusion. The stake makes identities costly to create: splitting one budget among a thousand sybils does not create a thousand units of voting weight, and detection burns capital rather than merely banning a disposable account. A falcon scout may spot patterns across an ocean of agents by dawn, but the attacker still pays for every unit of influence and risks losing the bond.
